headline: Daily market snapshot – September 29, 2026
summary: Major index futures edging lower Tuesday premarket as markets struggled to recover from Monday's broad yield- and oil-driven selloff. 10Y UST topped 5.25%, 30Y hit 5.58% (new highs since 2007/2004), gold slid 4% to $4,115.71 on rising real yields, Brent near $100 on Iran Hormuz standoff, DXY at two-month highs. headline: Gold slides 4% and the ten-year tops 5.25% — Saxo Market Quick Take September 29
summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.25% on September 29, a level last breached intraweek in 2007. Gold fell 4% to $4,115.71 per ounce, its lowest since early August, as rising real yields and oil-driven inflation pressured non-yielding metals. Silver fell more than 5% and platinum dropped over 3%, with precious metals miners broadly lower.

summary: Oil prices extended gains on September 29 as the ongoing US-Iran standoff at the Strait of Hormuz continued to outweigh Saudi Arabia's partial East-West pipeline flow restoration. Trump's rejection of Iran's ceasefire terms left traders pricing in sustained supply disruption.

Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal
Iran officials privately pessimistic about pre-November deal

Trump rejected seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal

headline: RBA hikes cash rate to 4.60%, fourth rise of 2026 and 15-year high
summary: Australia's Reserve Bank raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60% on September 29, the fourth hike of 2026 and the highest level in nearly 15 years, with a unanimous 9-0 vote. The board cited upside inflation risks materializing since August, driven by rising energy costs and resilient domestic demand. ANZ forecasts a fifth hike in November.
